title: Automate YouTube: Tools and Methods (2026 Guide)
summary: Automate YouTube uploads with YouTube Studio's scheduler, Activepieces, or API scripts. Each handles different levels of workflow complexity.
body_markdown:
## Stage 3: Script it with the YouTube Data API


When you control the Google credentials yourself, scripting means four moves: create a Cloud project, enable YouTube Data API v3, issue OAuth credentials, then call` videos.insert` and` commentThreads` . The default quota is 10,000 units a day, and that ceiling is where scripts usually break.


### Create the project and enable the API


In the Google Cloud console, create a project, open the API library, and enable YouTube Data API v3. Every project starts with 10,000 quota units a day, shared across every script and teammate using that project's credentials.


One runaway loop therefore locks out everyone else until the quota resets.


Check the date on any tutorial, because the cost of an upload has moved and old ones quote the old numbers. Before December 2025, one upload cost[1,600 units](https://www.blotato.com/blog/youtube-api-pricing) , so the default quota allowed six uploads a day.


From December 2025 to May 2026 it cost 100 units, which allowed about a hundred.


**From June 2026 it costs 1 unit** , so quota stops being the upload constraint. If a guide tells you to batch uploads to save quota, it predates the change.


### Authorise the YouTube Data API with OAuth scopes


Configure the OAuth consent screen, then create an OAuth client ID. A desktop-app client is enough for a script that runs under your own login. Request only the scopes you need:` youtube.upload` for publishing, and` youtube.force-ssl` for reading and moderating comments.


If you ask for the broad` youtube` scope when you only upload, the consent screen is harder to approve and a leaked token has more power than it should.


Keep the refresh token somewhere safe. If your consent screen is still in "Testing" status, Google expires that token after seven days, and a scheduler that worked on Friday fails the following week with an` invalid_grant` error.


### Upload a video and read comments


Call` videos.insert` with the video file and a` snippet` and` status` body. Set` privacyStatus` deliberately.


There's also an audit requirement: **videos uploaded through an API project that hasn't passed Google's compliance audit are locked to private.**


So a script can succeed, return a video ID, and publish nothing anyone can watch. Submit the audit before you promise a client a publishing schedule.


For reading,` commentThreads.list` takes a` videoId` and returns top-level comments with their replies attached. A list call costs 1 unit, so even at the default quota you can poll comments thousands of times a day.


Use` pageToken` to page through results instead of re-fetching, and store the last comment ID you saw so a nightly report counts only what is new.


Once uploads and comment reads work, wrap them in a scheduler and a log. The log matters more than the script, because quota and audit failures show up there first.
